raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-JOR-InnovativeStartupsSMEsFund2",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Geopolitical instability and regional macroeconomic shocks in the MENA region could suppress private capital flows and investor confidence, threatening capital mobilization targets.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Structure ISSF investments to provide matching co-investments on commercial non-subsidized terms to de-risk private VC entry, while serving as a strategic co-investment partner to regional/GCC funds.",
      "evidence": "Section I.A, para 1: Jordan’s small, open economy continues to face vulnerabilities tied to its position in a geopolitically volatile region."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "High-growth Jordanian startups may relocate headquarters to GCC or Western markets to access larger growth capital, reducing local economic and employment impact.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Contractually enforce Side Letters with partner VC funds requiring portfolio companies to maintain significant commercial operations and workforce footprint in Jordan.",
      "evidence": "Section I.B, para 7: Availability of long-term funding and market size in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries... prompt high-growth Jordanian startups to expand elsewhere"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "Expansion of ICT and technology startups supported by the fund could lead to improper management and disposal of e-waste, causing environmental pollution and health hazards.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Integrate E&S screening into sub-project approval, enforce e-waste management clauses in Fund legal documentation, and promote adoption of good e-waste recycling practices.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.C, para 77: SMEs’ supported activities may cause environmental impacts connected to mismanagement of e-waste, including pollution, Occupational Health and Safety"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Growing ICT startups could lack formal human resources policies, leading to labor standard violations, discrimination, or sexual harassment in the workplace.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement ESCP gap-filling measures aligning beneficiary practices with national labor law and ESS2, adopt workplace non-discrimination policies, and enforce anti-harassment standards.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.C, para 78: Additional labor risks related to ICT start-ups include terms and conditions of employment, discrimination, and sexual harassment"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "The existing Grievance Mechanism (GM) at ISSF may lack sufficient reach or specialized procedures to address SEA/SH complaints and broader stakeholder concerns effectively.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Enhance GM protocols to establish safe, confidential, survivor-centered uptake channels for SEA/SH and extend accessible grievance reporting mechanisms across all sub-projects.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.C, para 82: according to a recent E&S audit for ISSF, it was found that the GM system requires enhancement"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Over-concentration of investable capital into a single VC fund or startup could lead to disproportionate portfolio losses if the counterparty underperforms.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Incorporate strict nominal and percentage exposure caps in the Project Operations Manual (e.g., maximum US$5 million cap and no more than 15% loan size per fund).",
      "evidence": "Section II.D, para 34: To mitigate and manage concentration risks, the current ISSF Investment Strategy sets out the limit on ISSF investment in one VC fund."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "An acute shortage of pre-seed and seed financing could bottleneck the pipeline of deal-ready startups moving toward early and growth stage venture rounds.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Ring-fence approximately 30 percent of total investable capital under Component 1 specifically for pre-seed and seed stage funds, incubators, and accelerators.",
      "evidence": "Section II.D, para 33: pre-seed and seed funding are in short supply."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "ISSF and financial intermediaries may lack sufficient capacity to evaluate and manage Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) requirements and standard ESMS implementation.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Appoint dedicated E&S staff within the ISSF PMU, mandate that all recipient VC funds establish an approved ESMS, and provide continuous institutional capacity building.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.C, para 79: ISSF requires improved E&S risks and impacts management capacity, especially in the implementation of the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Private VC funds and startups could fail to comply with acceptable commercial procurement practices or misprice sub-contracts, causing fiduciary compliance failures.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Recruit a qualified procurement specialist for the PMU, outline explicit commercial practices in the POM, perform annual ex-post reviews, and engage independent technical auditors.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.B, para 73: ISSF shall satisfy itself with the reasonableness of the price of contracts awarded, through the hiring of independent auditors"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "The legal structure of ISSF as a Private Shareholding Company set to expire in 2029 conflicts with standard 10–12 year venture capital investment cycles.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Execute a legal amendment to ISSF's Articles of Association as an effectiveness condition to convert ISSF into an open-ended Private Shareholding Company.",
      "evidence": "Section II.D, para 30(vii): currently the ISSF Private Shareholding Company ‘ends’ in 2029"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Relying on external lead investors for due diligence under Component 2 co-investments could expose ISSF to flawed valuations or excessive aggregate exposure to single startups.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish strict double-exposure checks across Component 1 and 2 in the POM, cap co-investments at US$500,000, and ensure independent review by the Investment Committee.",
      "evidence": "Section II.D, para 36: consider the risks related to total exposure to the same startups (through Component 1 and Component 2)"
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Deep-seated social norms and systemic barriers could prevent female and youth entrepreneurs from equitably accessing early-stage risk capital.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Implement a Gender Action Plan with targeted outreach, mandate at least 20% female representation on the Board and Investment Committee, and target >=30% female-led/owned beneficiaries.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.C, para 78: there is a risk that they may not fully benefit if specific barriers to their participation are not effectively addressed."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Sub-project funding could inadvertently support business activities that are non-aligned with Paris Agreement objectives or increase national mitigation/adaptation vulnerabilities.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 2,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Update the ISSF Investment Strategy and POM to include universal Paris Alignment exclusion lists and counterparty/transaction screening procedures.",
      "evidence": "Section IV.A, para 56: ISSF Investment Strategy will be updated to amend the exclusion list with activities that are universally non-aligned from Paris Alignment perspective."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Geopolitical instability and regional macroeconomic shocks in the MENA region could suppress private capital flows and investor confidence, threatening capital mobilization targets.
risks.mitigation: Structure ISSF investments to provide matching co-investments on commercial non-subsidized terms to de-risk private VC entry, while serving as a strategic co-investment partner to regional/GCC funds.
risks.evidence: Section I.A, para 1: Jordan’s small, open economy continues to face vulnerabilities tied to its position in a geopolitically volatile region.

risks.description: High-growth Jordanian startups may relocate headquarters to GCC or Western markets to access larger growth capital, reducing local economic and employment impact.
risks.mitigation: Contractually enforce Side Letters with partner VC funds requiring portfolio companies to maintain significant commercial operations and workforce footprint in Jordan.
risks.evidence: Section I.B, para 7: Availability of long-term funding and market size in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries... prompt high-growth Jordanian startups to expand elsewhere

risks.description: Expansion of ICT and technology startups supported by the fund could lead to improper management and disposal of e-waste, causing environmental pollution and health hazards.
risks.mitigation: Integrate E&S screening into sub-project approval, enforce e-waste management clauses in Fund legal documentation, and promote adoption of good e-waste recycling practices.
risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 77: SMEs’ supported activities may cause environmental impacts connected to mismanagement of e-waste, including pollution, Occupational Health and Safety

risks.description: Growing ICT startups could lack formal human resources policies, leading to labor standard violations, discrimination, or sexual harassment in the workplace.
risks.mitigation: Implement ESCP gap-filling measures aligning beneficiary practices with national labor law and ESS2, adopt workplace non-discrimination policies, and enforce anti-harassment standards.
risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 78: Additional labor risks related to ICT start-ups include terms and conditions of employment, discrimination, and sexual harassment

risks.description: The existing Grievance Mechanism (GM) at ISSF may lack sufficient reach or specialized procedures to address SEA/SH complaints and broader stakeholder concerns effectively.
risks.mitigation: Enhance GM protocols to establish safe, confidential, survivor-centered uptake channels for SEA/SH and extend accessible grievance reporting mechanisms across all sub-projects.
risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 82: according to a recent E&S audit for ISSF, it was found that the GM system requires enhancement

risks.description: Over-concentration of investable capital into a single VC fund or startup could lead to disproportionate portfolio losses if the counterparty underperforms.
risks.mitigation: Incorporate strict nominal and percentage exposure caps in the Project Operations Manual (e.g., maximum US$5 million cap and no more than 15% loan size per fund).
risks.evidence: Section II.D, para 34: To mitigate and manage concentration risks, the current ISSF Investment Strategy sets out the limit on ISSF investment in one VC fund.

risks.description: An acute shortage of pre-seed and seed financing could bottleneck the pipeline of deal-ready startups moving toward early and growth stage venture rounds.
risks.mitigation: Ring-fence approximately 30 percent of total investable capital under Component 1 specifically for pre-seed and seed stage funds, incubators, and accelerators.
risks.evidence: Section II.D, para 33: pre-seed and seed funding are in short supply.

risks.description: ISSF and financial intermediaries may lack sufficient capacity to evaluate and manage Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) requirements and standard ESMS implementation.
risks.mitigation: Appoint dedicated E&S staff within the ISSF PMU, mandate that all recipient VC funds establish an approved ESMS, and provide continuous institutional capacity building.
risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 79: ISSF requires improved E&S risks and impacts management capacity, especially in the implementation of the World Bank Environmental and Social Standards

risks.description: Private VC funds and startups could fail to comply with acceptable commercial procurement practices or misprice sub-contracts, causing fiduciary compliance failures.
risks.mitigation: Recruit a qualified procurement specialist for the PMU, outline explicit commercial practices in the POM, perform annual ex-post reviews, and engage independent technical auditors.
risks.evidence: Section IV.B, para 73: ISSF shall satisfy itself with the reasonableness of the price of contracts awarded, through the hiring of independent auditors

risks.description: The legal structure of ISSF as a Private Shareholding Company set to expire in 2029 conflicts with standard 10–12 year venture capital investment cycles.
risks.mitigation: Execute a legal amendment to ISSF's Articles of Association as an effectiveness condition to convert ISSF into an open-ended Private Shareholding Company.
risks.evidence: Section II.D, para 30(vii): currently the ISSF Private Shareholding Company ‘ends’ in 2029

risks.description: Relying on external lead investors for due diligence under Component 2 co-investments could expose ISSF to flawed valuations or excessive aggregate exposure to single startups.
risks.mitigation: Establish strict double-exposure checks across Component 1 and 2 in the POM, cap co-investments at US$500,000, and ensure independent review by the Investment Committee.
risks.evidence: Section II.D, para 36: consider the risks related to total exposure to the same startups (through Component 1 and Component 2)

risks.description: Deep-seated social norms and systemic barriers could prevent female and youth entrepreneurs from equitably accessing early-stage risk capital.
risks.mitigation: Implement a Gender Action Plan with targeted outreach, mandate at least 20% female representation on the Board and Investment Committee, and target >=30% female-led/owned beneficiaries.
risks.evidence: Section IV.C, para 78: there is a risk that they may not fully benefit if specific barriers to their participation are not effectively addressed.

risks.description: Sub-project funding could inadvertently support business activities that are non-aligned with Paris Agreement objectives or increase national mitigation/adaptation vulnerabilities.
risks.mitigation: Update the ISSF Investment Strategy and POM to include universal Paris Alignment exclusion lists and counterparty/transaction screening procedures.
risks.evidence: Section IV.A, para 56: ISSF Investment Strategy will be updated to amend the exclusion list with activities that are universally non-aligned from Paris Alignment perspective.
